text:
marta: flag from user testing today: people were unsure whether the scorecard row approve icon applies to a single run or the whole prompt-set. They hovered and couldn't tell. Screenshot: https://img.redwood.ai/ps-approve-ambiguity.png ed: thanks — that's a good find. We currently show a small check icon with tooltip "Approve". We should make the primary affordance explicit text like "Approve run" and have a separate bulk action in the header. lin: accessibility point: icons-only buttons are ambiguous for assistive tech. If we add text, also ensure the visible text is truncated but full text available to screen readers via aria-label. Eg: ``. sam: UX suggestion: keep the compactness by showing text only on hover/focus and an abbreviated label otherwise. But that creates layout shift. Maybe show a glyph + short label (`Run`) and full label in tooltip/focus. marta: research preferred explicit verbs. They liked "Approve run" for single items and "Approve selected" for multi-select. Propose: change icon to a small pill that reads "Approve run" on desktop, and on narrow widths show a compact icon with `aria-label`. ed: also let's clarify keyboard flow: Enter opens diff, Space toggles selection, and `A` should open bulk approve modal (or snackbar). We should avoid `Enter` approving. lin: on screenreader announcements: when a user approves, have an assertive live region read "Approved 1 run. Undo." and when bulk approve happens read "Approved 3 runs. Undo." Keep numbers localized tokens. Debounce to avoid multiple messages if batch actions happen quickly. sam: small implementation snippet idea (for devs): ```
Approved 1 run 14 Undo
``` but we should pull copy from translations, not hardcode English. marta: behavior wise: prefer snackbar with undo that doesn't move focus. But the undo button must be keyboard-accessible and reachable via Tab. If we auto-focus snackbar, users navigating with keyboard lose their place. ed: agree. Instead of moving focus, we can add `role="status" aria-live="polite"` for non-critical messages and `assertive` for approvals so AT users hear it. Don't trap focus. lin: a11y nit: when opening a diff from a keyboard, focus should move into the diff panel and land on a heading that announces the test name and change count. Eg `h2 id="diff-title">Test A 14 3 changes`. Then the live region can optionally read a short sentence. sam: copy micro-nit: use verbs first in snackbars: "Approved 2 runs 14 Undo" instead of "2 runs approved" — this helps scanning. Also confirm pluralization tokens are correct for languages with complex plural rules. marta: agreed. Action items: marta -> update Figma with pill-style approve and compact mobile fallback; ed -> change keyboard mapping doc and top-right shortcuts menu; lin -> PR for aria-live + focus management and example markup; sam -> update copy tokens for snackbars and tooltip text. ux-bot: created task PROD-3777 "Scorecard: clarify approve affordance + keyboard + a11y" (https://tasks.redwood.ai/3777) assigned to marta and lin ed: one last thought: show a subtle separator between the inline approve pill and other meta (time, status) so it doesn't look like a tag. Keep tap target >=44px per touch guidelines. marta: good call. i'll push an updated prototype this afternoon and link it here. thanks everyone :sparkles:
